title: Side-by-side language references and multi-language code collections
description: Sites and documents that show the same construct, idiom or program in many languages at once: Learn X in Y Minutes, Programming-Idioms (with individual idioms mapped to concepts), Pascal Rigaux's "Syntax across languages" (per-construct anchors and per-language columns), the Wikipedia "Comparison of programming languages" family (per-section anchors), 99 Bottles of Beer, the Hello World Collection, PLEAC, Sample Programs, Exercism tracks and Wikibooks cross-language books. Rosetta Code and Hyperpolyglot have their own collections (rosetta-code-tasks, hyperpolyglot). Every "languages" list was derived from the site's own language index and mapped to catalog ids; languages without a catalog id are omitted.

resources.title: Learn X in Y Minutes — index of language tours
resources.notes: One-page annotated code tours (a single commented source file per language/tool), all following the same pattern: comments, primitives, variables, collections, control flow, functions, modules, classes. Per-language pages live at https://learnxinyminutes.com/<slug>/; the language list here covers the pages that map to catalog ids.

resources.title: adambard/learnxinyminutes-docs — source of the Learn X in Y Minutes pages
resources.notes: Markdown sources (one file per language plus translations); useful to see all tours side by side or diff them.

resources.title: Programming-Idioms — the same small task in many languages
resources.notes: ~370 idioms, each with a one-line specification and one or more implementations per language (Python, Java, Go, Rust, C++, C#, JS, Pascal, Haskell, Fortran, Ada, COBOL ...). Pascal entries are mostly Free Pascal/Delphi; "VB" is Visual Basic .NET; "Lisp" is Common Lisp.

resources.notes: Any language pair can be requested as /cheatsheet/<Lang1>/<Lang2>; a single language as /cheatsheet/<Lang>.
